### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via SysUserPermissionSet (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class), authorEnvironmentSets (symbol, a field of interface DelegableAdminScope), manageBindings (symbol, a field of interface DelegableAdminScope), adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections), authorEnvironmentSets (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_ADMIN_SCOPE_KEYS; a string literal in apply; a string literal in summary), manageBindings (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_ADMIN_SCOPE_KEYS; a string literal in apply; a string literal in summary), sales_user (literal, a string literal in fixture), /api/v1/security/my-delegable-scope (route, the route ledger binds it to client method security.describeDelegableScope))_
- `content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-metadata.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections), sales_user (literal, a string literal in fixture))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections), sales_user (literal, a string literal in fixture))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/positions.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_
- `content/docs/permissions/profiles.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class), PermissionSetSchema (symbol, a top-level const), authorEnvironmentSets (symbol, a field of interface DelegableAdminScope), manageBindings (symbol, a field of interface DelegableAdminScope), adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections), authorEnvironmentSets (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_ADMIN_SCOPE_KEYS; a string literal in apply; a string literal in summary), manageBindings (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_ADMIN_SCOPE_KEYS; a string literal in apply; a string literal in summary))_
- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via adminScope (literal, a string literal in sections))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retiredAfter (symbol, a field of const object permissionAdminScopeBindingAuthoringRemoved), retiredFromLoadPath (symbol, a field of const object permissionAdminScopeBindingAuthoringRemoved))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/security.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/security.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4cc310b88f0b85ef8a88cce2753420b8e06a16e4` — the merge of head `3854d1403f268d66b6ce39f7859e1fd52bbdccfe` into base `16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4cc310b88f0b85ef8a88cce2753420b8e06a16e4 && git checkout 4cc310b88f0b85ef8a88cce2753420b8e06a16e4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17 3854d1403f268d66b6ce39f7859e1fd52bbdccfe && git checkout -B drift-repro 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17 && git merge --no-ff 3854d1403f268d66b6ce39f7859e1fd52bbdccfe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 16abea88450be3c453a9e769445af341a956bd17` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The strip conversion is `permission-admin-scope-binding-authoring-removed` (`MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`, `retiredFromLoadPath`).    - The changeset adds `core` and `platform-objects` patch rows because both publish changed content.

7. **Landing terms.**
   - First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green, then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `needs:contract-review` stays on this PR until then.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3854d1403f268d66b6ce39f7859e1fd52bbdccfe`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #23488 (its body and all ten comments; the ruling of record is 6181988435, letter A, items 1–5; the dev's report is 6184471100), PR #23601's body and its 38-file list, the net diff of this head against `main` (merge-base `16abea884`; +1016 / −112), and the 45 check-runs on the head. Published schema is in the file list (`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, `contracts/security-service.ts`, `conversions/registry.ts`), which puts the face at this tier; no governed path is in the list. The ADR half is PR #23602 and is not judged here. Read-only: the diff was read with `git diff` against fetched refs, the GitHub records over REST; nothing was built, run or re-run.

Gates, read off the head: all 45 runs concluded — 37 `success`, 8 `skipped`, 0 failed. The five required contexts are `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core with all six shards, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard), as are Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Type Check · consumer gates, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, the single-writer and claim guards and the docs-drift flag. Skipped are the full-battery and opt-in jobs only: Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `AdminScopeSchema.manageBindings` and `AdminScopeSchema.authorEnvironmentSets` become `retiredKey()` tombstones on the `strictObject`: every value, the former default `false` included, is refused at the key's own path with the prescription, and the key's input type is the retired mark. RIGHT — ruling item 1. The prescription carries the ruled sentence verbatim ("Delete the key; a delegate's scope is placement, assignment and the allowlist"), opens with the backticked fully-qualified key, names `@objectstack/spec 18`, ADR-0049 and ADR-0090 D12, closes with the house `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence, and carries no tracker number. A parsed scope no longer materializes either default (pinned in `permission.test.ts`; the dogfood zoo asserts the served definition carries neither key).
2. Every door that parses a permission set narrows with it: the `permission` registry binding (`PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/:name` validates against it), `defineStack({ permissions })` with the `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 envelope, and `definePermissionSet()`. RIGHT — pinned in the new retirement test, each with a CONTROL that the same body without the keys passes.
3. D2 conversion `permission-admin-scope-binding-authoring-removed` in `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`: order 65 (the previous maximum is 64), inserted at its identifier's sort position and defined directly above the entry that follows it; `retiredFromLoadPath: true`; `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, the value the other newest-stable retirements in the 18 list carry. It strips both keys from every `permissions[].adminScope` whatever they hold, one notice per key, the notice path naming the set; the fixture carries four sets and `expectedNotices: 4`. RIGHT — ruling item 1's `registered` strip. A live author is refused, never rewritten (pinned); a stored `permission` row replays clean through `applyConversionsToStoredItem` and a built artifact through `applyConversions` with retired entries included (pinned, with a lit control that a scope which was always wrong is refused on both sides); idempotent by construction (`stripKeys`) and pinned anyway. The `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue` stage is not adopted, with the `email_template.isSystem` precedent named — right for a key whose residue the replayed strip heals.
4. `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `security/AdminScope:manageBindings` and `security/AdminScope:authorEnvironmentSets` (two files under `migrations/entries/retired-keys/`, named from the ids, spelled as `authorable-surface/security.json` spells them); one D3 semantic entry `permission-admin-scope-binding-authoring-retired` states the containment change with non-empty `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` and no backtick in `surface`; one `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment at order 97 (the previous maximum is 96), at its id's sort position. RIGHT — the generated `registry.ts` is gitignored, so nothing more is owed in the diff; the registration pins and both merge tests run under Test Core.
5. `DelegableAdminScope` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`) and plugin-security's `DelegableScopeReport` drop both fields, so `GET /api/v1/security/my-delegable-scope` reports `manageAssignments` as the scope's one action right. RIGHT — ruling item 1. The changeset's FROM → TO table names the endpoint; the `api-surface` snapshot is unaffected by design (it records export presence, not member sets); every Type Check lane and the consumer gates are green, and a tree-wide grep of the head finds no remaining typed reader of either field (the client dialog reads `placeableBusinessUnitIds` and `assignablePositions` only).
6. `definitionContainsStrictly` compares `includeSubtree`, `manageAssignments` and the allowlist only, on both sides. Two accept-set moves on the delegated `sys_user_position` and `sys_user_permission_set` writes: case (ii) — a delegate whose own scope carries an inert `true` can no longer hand out a scope otherwise EQUAL to its own; it answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, closing the live loosening the ruling named; case (i) reversed — a granted scope carrying a retired `true` (a stored row the strip has not yet rewritten) no longer out-reaches a delegate that lacks it. RIGHT — ruling item 2. Case (ii) is pinned on `code`, `status` and the message's first clause, beside a CONTROL in which the same delegate grants a scope narrower on the subtree axis; case (i) reversed is pinned too. The gate fixture `EAST_SCOPE` set both flags `true` on both sides before this diff, so the pins are new, not flipped assertions. `resolveHeldScopes` and `describeDelegableScope` stop reading the keys, and the `scopesCoverUser` JSDoc now says what the code does (it reads no flag).
7. `permissionSetDefinitionFromRow` (`@objectstack/core`) drops both keys from a legacy row's `admin_scope`, whatever they hold, before the ceremony's body reaches `saveMetaItem`. RIGHT — ruling item 3 made this conditional on a measurement, and the report supplies it: the save replays no conversion (a 17.x-shaped row answered `422 INVALID_METADATA` at `adminScope.manageBindings`; the same row without the keys saved). Pinned for `false`, `true` and a non-boolean value, with a CONTROL that the body with the key kept is refused at exactly `['adminScope', 'manageBindings']`. The fixed two-name list is documented as this retirement's own D2 strip applied at the one seam the seam table does not reach, naming the conversion id, and the comment says why it is written down rather than derived. `organization-ownership-apply.ts` is untouched, as the claim required.

Public-surface and generated-surface changes, each judged:

8. `authorable-surface/security.json`: both rows become `[RETIRED]`; `authorable-defaults/security.json`: both default rows go. RIGHT for the tombstone route (the row stays, marked). `authorable-surface.base.json` still lists both keys unmarked — RIGHT: that file is the deletion gate's anchor, written only by `--update-base`, never by a retirement PR.
9. `liveness/permission.json`: `adminScope` stays `live`, its evidence rewritten to the two assignment doors and the three containment axes, with a RE-VERIFIED note. The ledger holds no drilled rows for the scope's keys, so no `dead` row is owed and none is orphaned. RIGHT — Spec property liveness is `success`.
10. The generated reference `content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` is regenerated: both rows read `never` / `[REMOVED]` with the prescription, and the `adminScope` type string on `PermissionSet` narrows to the four live keys. RIGHT — hand-edits are absent, as the auto-gen boundary requires.
11. `permission.form.ts` help text names the four live keys; the `en` bundle is regenerated from it, and the `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` `helpText` values are hand-edited. RIGHT — translated-locale values are hand-written by rule, no key was added or dropped, and `check:i18n` sits inside the green Lint & Repo Gates. The form keeps its one `adminScope` json widget; there was no per-key input to cut.
12. Position 3 text, docs accuracy with no contract change: the two docs sentences (`delegated-administration.mdx` action-flag and strict-containment rows; `permission-sets.mdx` strict-containment paragraph), the showcase's seven sentences plus its two deleted keys, the spec JSDoc and `.describe()` strings, the ledger note, the two plugin-security comments, the `meta-write-capability.ts` docstring, and `docs/design/permission-model.md`. RIGHT. The strict-containment row now states the three axes exactly as the code compares them. The showcase's new claim that `showcase_guest_portal` reaches people through the `client_portal_user` position is TRUE on the head (`examples/app-showcase/src/security/positions.ts`, lines 98–101 declare that position with `permissionSets: ['showcase_guest_portal']`). `docs/design/` is not a governed surface.
13. The tree-scoped absence pin `admin-scope-binding-authoring-retirement.test.ts`, registered in `vitest.repo-tests.json` (so it runs under `test:repo`, which Test Core runs): it walks the five roots with the same seed spelling as the `rls-tags` precedent, and its radius is declared for `@objectstack/spec` in `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and mirrored in `turbo.json` (`packages/**` per extension, `examples/*/src/**/*.ts`, the non-code `examples/**` extensions, `content/**`, `skills/**`, `scripts/**`). It excludes only the kit's own files, each with its reason and no allowlist file; the matcher has anti-vacuity cases and the walk has visit-count floors. RIGHT. A tree-wide grep of the head finds no authoring of either key outside the kit; the remaining mentions are prose, the governed ADR-0086 row (PR #23602's) and one string literal in the legacy-catalog testkit, which the walk's string masking ignores by design.
14. The two `@ts-expect-error` lines are in a file the spec `typecheck` script compiles (`check:test-typecheck` runs inside it); TypeScript Type Check is `success`, so they are not phantom checks. RIGHT.

Nothing in the diff was judged WRONG.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23488-admin-scope-binding-authoring-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor`, `@objectstack/core: patch`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`. RIGHT. The two ruled packages publish a BREAKING narrowing, and `minor` is the house level inside the 18 pre-window (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major`; a `yes` declaration takes at least `minor`); the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO table and the one-line fix are present; exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker, `registered`, names the D2 and the D3 ids. `core` publishes the mapper fix and `platform-objects` the four help texts — both changed content, both `patch`. `metadata-core` changes a docstring only and rightly carries no row. No `skip-changeset`. Check Changeset is `success`.

`Clause-②:` line — the PR body declares `Clause-②: yes`; the changeset carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, where the ADR-0087 gate reads the arm. Both are well-formed under the closed grammar and match what the diff publishes: a published spec accept-set narrows. The claim (6182195274) and the ruling both say `yes (narrowing)`. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

The report's `open_questions` is empty. Its deviations, acceptance notes and out-of-scope findings, each answered or escalated:

1. File surface beyond the claim's list (`docs/design/permission-model.md`, the showcase tour doc, the dogfood zoo test, six plugin-security fixtures, the removal-version pin's JOIN row, `vitest.repo-tests.json`, the generated `authorable-*` and reference files) — ANSWERED: each is a necessary carrier of the ruled change or a generator's output, each with its reason in the PR body; none widens scope.
2. Changeset rows beyond the two ruled packages — ANSWERED: see ②.
3. PR-body `Clause-②: yes` without the arm — ANSWERED: see ②; the arm lives in the changeset, where the gate reads it.
4. Local verification narrowed after the lock-pressure note (consumer suites, the cli integration tier, metadata-core, the showcase validate were not run locally) — ANSWERED: the per-PR check-runs cover them; Test Core 6/6, every Type Check lane and the consumer gates are `success`.
5. Ruling item 4, objectui: Studio's two switches, help strings, i18n keys and pin test are objectstack-ai/objectui#12406, not this PR, and this PR moves no pin. The report's typing reproduction of `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx` at pin `b9814b334d` against this branch's spec dist compiled, with a lit CONTROL (a literal retired key fails TS2322; `DelegableAdminScope.manageBindings` fails TS2339). A full objectui build at the pin is NOT MEASURED, and Console Pin Gate is full-battery only (skipped on this head). ESCALATED AS A WATCH, not a block: the ruling itself sequences the objectui landing "before or with the `.objectui-sha` move", so this head may land first; until objectui#12406 lands, a Studio switch flip meets the schema's refusal with the prescription (422), the ruled loud behaviour; the first full-battery Console Pin Gate on `main` after landing is the spec lane's to read.
6. Out-of-repo stored rows and consumers — NOT MEASURED, as every reading on the card said; in-repo coverage is complete: the D2 strip on the rehydration seams, the mapper on the ceremony seam, the tombstones at every authoring door.
7. The dogfood `showcase-permission-zoo` file is not in per-PR CI (the shards are skipped); the report ran it on the merged head, 10 passed. ANSWERED; the full battery on `main` is its carrier.
8. `check:platform-checklist` reds with 8 ABSENT SYMBOL anchors — ANSWERED: reproduced identically on `main` without this diff, none of the named anchors is in this PR's file list, and the daily watchdog is the carrier; outside this card's three classes.
9. `legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.ts` still names both keys in a column description — ANSWERED: it models the retired `sys_permission_set` column as it was, and it is a string literal the absence walk masks, so it is not an authoring.
10. Three PROSPECTIVE sentences about a `guest` bind door (`builtin-positions.ts`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`, the `permission-sets.mdx` wildcard-ban line) left in place — ANSWERED: ADR-0138 D3 item 4 assigns that door for later; they are not false on `main`.
